901: from the base of βάσις; profound (as going down), literally or figuratively:--deep, very early.
902: a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of βάσις; a palm twig (as going out far):--branch.
903: of Hebrew origin (בִּלְעָם); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher):--Balaam.
904: of Hebrew origin (בָּלָק); Balak, a Moabite:--Balac.
905: probably remotely from βάλλω (as a depository); a pouch (for money):--bag, purse.
906: a primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense):--arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare ῥίπτω.
907: from a derivative of βάπτω; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism:--Baptist, baptize, wash.
909: from βαπτίζω; ablution (ceremonial or Christian):--baptism, washing.
910: from βαπτίζω; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner:--Baptist.
911: a primary verb; to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye):--dip.
912: of Chaldee origin (גָּאוֹן and אֲבַגְתָא); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite:--Barabbas.
913: of Hebrew origin (בָּרָק); Barak, an Israelite:--Barak.
914: of Hebrew origin (בֶּרֶכְיָה); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an Israelite:--Barachias.
915: of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e. non-Greek):--barbarian(-rous).
916: from βαρύς; to weigh down (figuratively):--burden, charge, heavy, press.
918: of Chaldee origin (בַּר and תַּלְמַי); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomæus, a Christian apostle:--Bartholomeus.
919: of Chaldee origin (בַּר and יְהוֹשׁוּעַ); son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite:--Barjesus.
920: of Chaldee origin (בַּר and יוֹנָה); son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite:--Bar-jona.
921: of Chaldee origin (בַּר and נְבִיא); son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite:--Barnabas.
922: probably from the same as βάσις (through the notion of going down; compare βάθος); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority:--burden(-some), weight.
923: of Chaldee origin (בַּר and probably צְבָא); son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites:--Barsabas.
924: of Chaldee origin (בַּר and טָמֵא); son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite:--Bartimæus.
926: from the same as βάρος; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave:--grievous, heavy, weightier.
927: from βαρύς and τιμή; highly valuable:--very precious.
928: from βάσανος; to torture:--pain, toil, torment, toss, vex.
931: perhaps remotely from the same as βάσις (through the notion of going to the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture:--torment.
932: from βασιλεύς; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively):--kingdom, + reign.
933: neuter of βασίλειος; a palace:--king's court.
935: probably from βάσις (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively):--king.
936: from βασιλεύς; to rule (literally or figuratively):--king, reign.
937: from βασιλεύς; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent:--king's, nobleman, royal.
939: from (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot:--foot.
940: akin to φάσκω; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations):--bewitch.
941: perhaps remotely derived from the base of βάσις (through the idea of removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.):--bear, carry, take up.
942: of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub:--bramble, bush.
943: of Hebrew origin (בַּת); a bath, or measure for liquids:--measure.
945: from (a proverbial stammerer) and λόγος; to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously:--use vain repetitions.
946: from βδελύσσω; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry:--abomination.
948: from a (presumed) derivative of (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry):--abhor, abominable.
949: from the base of βάσις (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively):--firm, of force, stedfast, sure.
952: from the base of βάσις and (a threshold); accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked:--profane (person).
954: of Chaldee origin (by parody on בַּעַל זְבוּב); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan:--Beelzebub.
955: of Hebrew origin (בְּלִיַּעַל); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan:--Belial.
956: from βάλλω; a missile, i.e. spear or arrow:--dart.
957: neuter of a compound of a derivative of βάλλω (used for the comparative of ἀγαθός); better:--very well.
958: of Hebrew origin (בִּנְיָמִין); Benjamin, an Israelite:--Benjamin.
959: from a provincial form of φέρω and νίκη; victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family:--Bernice.
960: perhaps a provincial from a derivative of πέραν (Perœa, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line); Berœa, a place in Macedonia:--Berea.
961: from Βέροια; a Berœoean or native of Berœa:--of Berea.
962: of Hebrew origin (בַּיִת and עֲבָרָה); ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan:--Bethabara.
963: of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine:--Bethany.
964: of Chaldee origin (compare בַּיִת and חֵסֵד); house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem:--Bethesda.
965: of Hebrew origin (בֵּית לְעַפְרָה); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine:--Bethlehem.
966: of Chaldee origin (compare בַּיִת and צַיָּד); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine:--Bethsaida.
967: of Chaldee origin (compare בַּיִת and פַּג); fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine:--Bethphage.
968: from the base of βάσις; a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal:--judgment-seat, set (foot) on, throne.
970: probably akin to βίος (through the idea of vital activity); force:--violence.
971: from βία; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized:--press, suffer violence.
973: from βιάζω; a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic:--violent.
974: a diminutive of βιβλίον; a booklet:--little book.
975: a diminutive of βίβλος; a roll:--bill, book, scroll, writing.
976: properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing:--book.
977: a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of βόσκω); to eat:--eat.
978: of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia:--Bithynia.
979: a primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood:--good, life, living.
981: from βιόω; living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode):--manner of life.
982: from a derivative of βιόω; relating to the present existence:--of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life.
984: a primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure:--hurt.
985: from (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit:--bring forth, bud, spring (up).
986: perhaps the same as the base of βλαστάνω; Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa:--Blastus.
987: from βλάσφημος; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously:--(speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil.
988: from βλάσφημος; vilification (especially against God):--blasphemy, evil speaking, railing.
989: from a derivative of βλάπτω and φήμη; scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God):--blasphemer(-mous), railing.
990: from βλέπω; vision (properly concrete; by implication, abstract):--seeing.
991: a primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively):--behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed. Compare ὀπτάνομαι.
992: from βάλλω; fit to be cast (i.e. applied):--must be put.
993: of Chaldee origin (בֵּן and רְגַז); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles:--Boanerges.
994: apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way):--cry.
995: from βοάω; a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.):--cry.
996: from βοηθός; aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel:--help.
997: from βοηθός; to aid or relieve:--help, succor.
998: from βοή and theo (to run); a succorer:--helper.
999: akin to βαθύνω; a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern:--ditch, pit.
